title: Libyan Arab Republic
capsule: The Libyan Arab Republic was the state founded on 1 September 1969 when a group of young officers led by Colonel Muammar Gaddafi overthrew King Idris I in a bloodless coup, abolishing the Senussi monarchy. Governed by a Revolutionary Command Council, it pursued pan-Arab nationalism, expelled remaining foreign military bases, and nationalised much of the oil sector that underwrote a new welfare state. The republic gave way on 2 March 1977 when the General People's Congress proclaimed the Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya, recasting the polity under Gaddafi's 'state of the masses' doctrine.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Libya's international borders are defined by colonial treaties (with Italy, France, Britain, and Egypt) and are internationally recognized; no territorial ambiguity affects the dataset geometry, though the polity's functional control of southern desert regions was at times nominal.
